notes:
Nebraska's franchise tax is the levy of Neb. Rev. Stat. § 77-3802, and its subjects are financial institutions: the statute imposes it "for the privilege of doing business in this state" on "all financial institutions with business locations in this state", measured on average deposits. A default LLC is not a financial institution, and the Department of Revenue's own pass-through entity tax FAQ states the classification that keeps it out of every corporate-style levy: an eligible partnership includes any entity, including an LLC, treated as a partnership for federal income tax purposes. applies is therefore false, on the statute and the Department's pages rather than on a silence.
collectedWithAnnualReport is null: no franchise-type levy remains for a default LLC, and root states.json carries annual_report_fee 25 for Nebraska, the Secretary of State's biennial report filing fee, a separate payment with no tax to overlap. Nebraska's corporate income tax applies to corporations, not to partnership-classified LLCs.
stateIncomeTax: members owe Nebraska individual income tax on pass-through income. The Department's rate chronology states that for taxable years beginning on or after January 1, 2025, and before January 1, 2026, the tax rate is 5.20% applied on all Nebraska taxable income (the schedule's top bracket for 2025); the same chronology shows the bracket structure is being compressed by the same legislation that compresses the PTET rate. Nebraska offers a pass-through entity tax election: the Department's FAQ names the eligible entities (partnerships and S corporations, with an eligible partnership including any LLC treated as a partnership) and publishes the PTET rate schedule - 5.20% for 2025, 4.55% for 2026, 3.99% for 2027 and after.
needsReview: The PTET's imposing statute was not read on nebraskalegislature.gov (the Department's FAQ carries the election and its rate schedule); the franchise tax's subject class is grounded in the statute itself.
